Subject: Renewal + capacity increase: pricing options for Q4

Vanessa —

Our renewal is coming up end of August and we expect a material uptick in inference volume when we roll out the new triage model in September. Before we lock the procurement cycle, procurement has a few asks: can you provide firm pricing options for (A) a 12-month renewal at current commit, (B) a 12-month renewal with a 2x commit, and (C) an 18-month renewal with a staged commit increase? They also asked whether Redwood can offer a short-term price hold while we finish internal approvals.

High level: we want to keep our unit cost contained while covering the expected usage spike. Happy to jump on a 30-min call next week to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Olivia Grant
Head of AI Platform
Grayline Health

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the context and timeline. I've attached a short deck and a pricing model that lays out three rows matching A/B/C you described. Early notes:
- 12mo/current commit: small discount (5%) for early renewal + standard volume tiers.
- 12mo/2x commit: deeper discount (12–15%) plus eligibility for 1-time usage credit if you hit the 2x in first 3 months.
- 18mo/staged: best blended unit price but requires a minimum commitment floor for first 6 months.

On price-hold: procurement asks for a 60–90 day hold window. I can offer a 60-day price-hold on any proposed quote while approvals are outstanding; beyond that I need approval from finance for a 90-day hold.

I've attached pricing_model_v2.xlsx for the math and a sample SOW sketch. Can we schedule a call on Tuesday (7/14) 10am PT?

Best,

Marissa / Marcus / Rishi —

Looping you in on Grayline's asks. Highlights and proposed concessions to discuss before Tuesday call:
1) Offer A (12mo/current): 5% list discount; auto-renew clause; no credits.
2) Offer B (12mo/2x commit): 15% list discount; one-time bridging credit of $25k applied if 2x usage observed within 90 days; flexibility to convert to dedicated pool after 6 months.
3) Offer C (18mo/staged): 18% blended discount; commit floor of 60% of projected month-1 usage for first 6 months; we provide a $40k onboarding credit and schedule a quarterly QBR.

Price-hold request: propose we commit to a 60-day hold from quote date; finance has to sign off for 90 days.

Please propose edits — I want a clean ask we can present to procurement.

- Vanessa

(On call: I plan to push for Offer B as our primary and Offer C if they want term certainty.)

Vanessa / Team —

Thanks for the options. Procurement's constraints: capital approval window runs through mid-September. We can accept a 60-day price-hold but will need a 90-day hold if the vendor can provide a one-time credit to offset our risk (we'd need the credit to be refundable if we fail to execute on agreed commit). Is Redwood open to a refundable transitional credit? Also, can the staged commit include a cap on overage rates for the first 6 months?

For clarity: our preferred commercial outcome is either Offer B (2x commit) with flexibility, or Offer C if the blended price is inside our budget.

Procurement asked that final SOW reflect the credit mechanics and any refund clauses.

- Grayline Procurement

Team —

Finance approved the following concessions to keep the deal moving:
- Price-hold: approve 60-day hold standard. Approve 90-day hold only with a refundable bridging credit up to $30k.
- Offer B (recommended): 14% list discount + $30k refundable transitional credit applied as a bill credit and refundable pro rata if Grayline reduces committed usage within first 4 months. Add overage cap for months 1–6 at current list +10%.
- Offer C: can keep 18% blended if Grayline signs an 18-month SOW with 45% minimum first-6-month floor; onboarding credit of $40k non-refundable (applied to first invoice) and QBRs.

I've redlined the SOW and attached Grayline_SOW_v3.pdf with the refund language and overage cap in section 3.4. Vanessa — please send the revised quote to procurement and request signature.

Marissa Cole
